newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Sept 18.

text.p: Copper ended an uncertain LME session with modest gains but oil rose on continuing U.S.-Iraq tensions while wheat firmed on a technical recovery.
The CRB index closed 0.22 points higher at 244.4.

Copper prices closed slightly higher as an easing trend in nearby spreads was partially reversed in the afternoon. Copper's cash/three months spread momentarily traded at a $2 contango - the first time the benchmark spread has been in contango since January 1995. At its peak in December 1995 the backwardation was some $330. But spread premiums have been under pressure for some time, and this was exacerbated after Monday's "third Wednesday" September pricing when previously tight dates fell out of the market's price structure. The market is long of the nearby dates through to October, with a $5 contango prevailing, which offset temporarily the backwardations at the rear of the spread. The cash/threes contango proved to be shortlived, as conditions were thin and some of the intermediate dates moved back into backwardation. However, cash/threes was only showing a $2 backwardation at the close, against Monday's $8/9. Forward business was mostly routine, with prices climbing off the lows as a 1,475-tonne decline in stocks was expected to be followed by further drawdowns. But the going became sticky overhead and last business was at $1,870, up $5 a tonne from Monday's kerb.
Aluminium notched up another two-year low, but the nadir of $1,411 induced some light trade buying and short-covering which temporarily halted the general decline of the last week.
But with stocks up 7,400 tonnes and expected to continue rising in the short-term the market is projected testing $1,400. Last business today was at $1,416.50, a $1.50 gain from Monday.
Nickel rose from the low in the afternoon, but was depressed after Monday's technical sell-off. LME stocks rose 510 tonnes while the Inco dispute is not a supportive factor at present.
Levels below $7,400 attracted some bargain-hunting buying, however, and the market closed at a steadier $7,430/40 a tonne.
Lead attempted a mini-rally this afternoon, with the market oversold, although the recovery was not enough to lift prices back into the plus column, traders said.
Charts are bearish under $800 and there is the possibility of further fund sales. By the kerb prices were retreating once more and last trade was at $772, a $13 loss from yesterday.

Zinc again encountered reasonable trade support on the dip below $1,020, which helped the market move higher in slow conditions. Last three months business was at $1,025, up $7 from the previous kerb.
COMEX December gold settled 20 cents lower at $386.10 an ounce, traded $387.00 to $386.00. The market soon bounced back from resistance at $387.00. London gold ended at $383.30/383.80.

CBOT wheat futures closed mostly firmer on a technical recovery tied to signals the market was oversold. A strong rally in soybean futures and firm corn values also boosted prices. Wheat futures closed 1/4 cent per bushel lower to five cents higher, with September down 1/4 at $4.23. December was 1-1/2 cents higher at $4.18-1/2.

NYMEX crude oil prices ended higher Tuesday after bullish news in the U.S.-Iraqi conflict triggered short covering, and pulled crude out of negative territory, said traders. Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said the United States was beefing up its military presence in the Middle East Gulf to launch another military strike against Iraq country. October crude oil settled up 12 cents at $23.31 a barrel after rising as high as $23.73 and falling as low as $22.97. NYMEX crude oil prices have been on a roller-coaster ride after being sent near the post-Gulf War high of $25.70 following military incursions by Saddam Hussein's troops into northern Kurdish regions in Iraq. October crude fell more than $1.00 Monday following an unsubstantiated report that the U.S. had asked Saudi Arabia to increase oil ouput. The report was denied by Middle East Gulf sources and U.S. State Department officials.

CSCE world sugar futures settled a heavily-traded session lower, but trade scale-down buying held the October contract above nearby support and buoyed prices off the lows by the close, market sources said. October sank 0.14 on the day to close at 11.43, having traded from 11.52 to 11.30. March ended off 0.13 at 11.28, while the back months settled off 0.08 to 0.06. LIFFE white sugar futures also settled down sharply, with losses in New York contributing to weakness in London. Spot December finished $5.40 lower to $327.00. The back months ended $4.70 to $2.20 lower.
